summary: Clackamas County, OR ODF lookout: 1914 crow's nest, 1951 tower, staffed into the 1980s, removed 2001; no source describes what remains today.

facts.design: Treated timber tower with L-4 cab and a ground cabin for living quarters (1951)
facts.status_note: Superstructure too rotten to save; removed in 2001. No source describes the site now.

events.note: Men of the Clackamas-Marion Fire Patrol Association working from the High Camp lookout station (Morning Oregonian, August 1914)
Tree crow's nest built; the first structure on the site
Fire spotted from the station, 26 miles from a settlement
Eight miles of telephone line built to the lookout; the 1915 State Forester report says the permanent lookout at High Camp gave excellent results
Patrol airplane located a fire and dropped a message that fell within a few feet of the tower
Ed Woodworth in charge of the lookout station during the summer
Road access: 1.7-mile extension from the end of a logging road
Tower with L-4 cab built; the 1951-52 district reports say 100 feet, the registers say 90 feet
Lookout painted; metal roof replaced with cedar shingles
U.S. Geological Survey station description: not occupied
Superstructure too rotten to salvage; taken down and listed as destroyed in 2001

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The two registers say the 1951 tower was 90 feet (27.4 m); the 1951 and 1952 district annual reports on the Forest Lookouts page say 100 feet (30.5 m). The record keeps 100 feet because it comes from the agency's own reports. The story gives both figures.

A 1957 U.S. Geological Survey station description says not occupied, while firelookout.com says the lookout was staffed into the 1980s. The sources do not say whether the 1957 entry covers one day or the whole year.

notes_for_editor: The brief's height 30.5 m is the 100-foot figure from the district reports; the registers say 90 feet, so the story gives both. No source read describes the site today. The Cascade District listing could not be read (SSL error) and a 1984 Facebook post could not be opened. Used 2 WebSearch and about 4 page reads.
